protectedRevelations: Detailed compact economics, legal mechanisms and implementation recommendations

scenes.title: Free code, unequal power
scenes.viewerPurpose: Make the distinctive idea or tension understandable on first hearing. Introduce the book-specific proposal clearly and leave its fuller explanation for reading.
scenes.composition: A developer carries open code away from a recognized name
addOrChange: Keep the code copy distinct from the service identity and add a blank proposed agreement.

cues.narration: Open code can be copied; the trust behind a familiar name is harder to share.
cues.visualAction: Move the code copy while the trusted public name remains behind.

cues.narration: The Licence and the Shared Name proposes a way for independent organizations to share that trust.
cues.visualAction: Place the proposed shared-name agreement beside the freely usable code.

scenes.title: What a licence leaves open
scenes.viewerPurpose: See why permission alone may not let work continue Notice where power stays despite open code
scenes.composition: A developer holds usable code outside a busy service entrance
addOrChange: Remove the many legal tabs and retain one customer queue and support contact.

cues.narration: It follows the gap between permission to copy and the support needed to keep building.
cues.visualAction: The code opens independently while the customer queue stays elsewhere.

cues.narration: The code may be open while customers, reputation, and reliable services stay in a few hands.
cues.visualAction: Show the service support and reputation attached to the entrance.

scenes.title: A shared name
scenes.viewerPurpose: Wonder how a shared name might help Consider cooperation that leaves people free
scenes.composition: Two independent operators review a proposed shared-name agreement
addOrChange: Add a second operator, mark the agreement Proposal, and leave signatures blank.

cues.narration: The book then investigates a proposed compact for organizations sharing one public name.
cues.visualAction: Set the proposed obligations between the two operators.

cues.narration: Could organizations share that trust while keeping their code open and their own choices free?
cues.visualAction: Keep separate workspaces and open code visible beneath one shared name.

scenes.title: Who can keep building
scenes.viewerPurpose: Connect the question to contributors and maintainers Ask who owes what to a community name
scenes.composition: Contribution history stays beside the open code and proposed agreement
addOrChange: Add maintenance and service notes without a winning legal outcome.

cues.narration: Maintainers, founders, and contributors meet a problem a licence alone cannot settle.
cues.visualAction: Bring the contribution record into the operators’ discussion.

cues.narration: Who should carry the obligations attached to a name everyone helped make valuable?
cues.visualAction: Leave responsibility for the shared name visibly under review.
